title: Power Electronics
summary: Device characteristics (SCR, TRIAC, GTO, IGBT, MOSFET), rectifier and converter output formulas, choppers, inverters, drives.
definitions: SCR
PNPN, 3 junctions; turned on by gate pulse, latches, turns off when current < holding current.
Latching current
Minimum anode current to stay on just after triggering (> holding current).
Holding current
Minimum anode current to keep conducting.
TRIAC
Two SCRs in anti-parallel with one gate; AC power control (dimmers, fan regulators); triggered by DIAC.
GTO
Thyristor that can be turned off by negative gate current.
IGBT
MOSFET-like voltage-controlled input with bipolar-like low conduction loss; inverters and drives.
Chopper
DC→DC converter controlling average output by duty cycle.
Inverter
DC→AC converter (VSI/CSI), output controlled by PWM.
Cycloconverter
AC→AC at a different (usually lower) frequency without a DC link.
Free-wheeling diode
Gives inductive load current a path, clamping output at zero and improving pf.
formulas: pulse number × f (6-pulse on 50 Hz → 300 Hz)
facts: SCR turn-on methods: gate (normal), forward breakover, dv/dt, thermal, light. Gate triggering is the reliable one.
RC snubber protects against dv/dt; series inductor against di/dt.
MOSFET has the highest switching frequency (majority carrier); SCR slowest.
Ripple factor: half-wave 1.21, full-wave 0.482. Rectification efficiency: 40.6% and 81.2%.
Full converter acts as an inverter for α > 90° (HVDC inverter, regenerative braking).
Forced commutation is needed for SCRs on DC (choppers, inverters).
Single-phase full converter input pf ≈ 0.9 cos α (highly inductive load).
Schottky diode: low forward drop (~0.3 V), negligible reverse recovery.
Online UPS feeds the load from the inverter continuously (double conversion).
traps: Latching current > holding current (not the reverse).
Centre-tap rectifier PIV is 2V_m; bridge PIV is V_m.
Boost output is V_in/(1 − D) — at D = 0.5 output doubles.
